newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius index rises for 16 consecutive sessions.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius index rises for 16 consecutive sessions.

text.p: The Semdex at the Mauritius bourse stretched its upward trend to 16 consecutive trading sessions on Wednesday, rising 2.51 points to 363.60 in higher volume which was seen bolstered by foreign investors.
Transactions totalled 25.86 million rupees on 1,290,351 shares from 6.07 million rupees on 249,931 shares on Monday.
The Mauritius bourse trades on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.
"Leading shares again drove the Semdex upward and were the targets of buying interests," one broker said, referring to stocks in the banking and commercial sectors.

Brokers attributed the soaring volume to foreign investors trading in leading shares such as New Mauritius Hotels and State Bank of Mauritius. New Mauritius Hotels lost 30 cents to 32 rupees on 203,443 shares.
State Bank of Mauritius shares went up by 20 cents to 11 rupees on 597,700 shares, hitting another all time high and extending their gains to 18.3 percent over the past month.
Analysts said State Bank, which enjoys a very good assessment among investors, is a favourite buying target of international investors.
Air Mauritius rose for the first time since late December after the national carrier reported an 86 percent slump in its pre-tax profit for the six months ending 30 September, 1996.
Air Mauritius which had lost some 13 percent since the result release, edged up by 10 cents to 43.50 rupees on 15,530 shares.
Commerce-based Courts surged by its maximum permitted 40 cents to 6.40 rupees on 27,839 shares in anticipation that the giant retailing concern made good sales during the Christmas period.
Mauritius Commercial Bank was unchanged at 82 rupees on 38,832 shares and hotel concern Sun Resorts was 30 cents higher to 40.10 rupees on 41,500 shares.
Sugar-based Mon Tresor Mon Desert climbed 10 cents to 39.60 rupees on 1,500 shares and Mauritius Union Assurance was up 80 cents to 29.20 rupees on 1,550 shares.
